title: MCE as 4th Pareto Objective in NSGA-II GA
source: brain-cycle-58 + Khairy et al. 2026 MDPI Information doi:10.3390/info17010056
motivation: The 2026 uncertainty-aware NBA paper shows Maximum Calibration Error (MCE) directly predicts betting profitability: poorly calibrated tails (MCE > 0.08) cause Kelly over-staking on the least reliable predictions. Current GA optimizes Brier + ROI + Sharpe (3 objectives). Adding MCE as a 4th Pareto dimension forces evolution to select models calibrated even in extreme probability regions (>0.75 or <0.25). This is where systematic edge is lost vs. bookmakers who clip lines at high odds.

technique.name: MCE (Maximum Calibration Error) Pareto Objective
technique.mce_definition: max over 10 bins of |mean(predicted_prob in bin) - mean(actual_outcome in bin)|
technique.expected_brier_delta: -0.001 to -0.003 indirect via tail calibration pressure
technique.expected_roi_delta: +1% to +2% fewer blown Kelly decisions on miscalibrated tails

implementation_steps: 1. In hf-space/app.py evaluate_individual(): add mce_score = compute_mce(y_pred_proba, y_test, n_bins=10)
2. In nsga2_rank(): expand fitness tuple from (brier, -roi, -sharpe) to (brier, -roi, -sharpe, mce)
5. Pareto front selection: minimize all 4 objectives simultaneously
cross_project_applicability: DIRECT — political GA can adopt same pattern; political_calibration.py Cat23 already tracks ECE/MCE as features (added cycle 58)
paper_citation: Khairy et al. (2026). Uncertainty-Aware Machine Learning for NBA Forecasting in Digital Betting Markets. MDPI Information 17(1):56.
